title: CostPilot — continuous workload profiling, heuristic scoring, and guarded batching apply
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We need an always-on recommendation engine (internal name: CostPilot) that profiles live workloads to produce per-workload batching + caching parameter suggestions, scores candidate configs by cost/latency trade-offs, and applies changes using a guarded rollout that can automatically revert on regressions. The motivation is to automate mundane tuning work, reduce per-token cost for common workloads, and keep latency SLO regressions within an acceptable bound.

Goals and success metrics:
- Achieve median cost-per-token reduction of 20–35% across targeted workloads within 2 weeks of rollout.
- No more than 2% of workloads may see >5% increase in p95 latency after guarded apply.
- Rollback or auto-revert must trigger for any workload with >5% error rate increase or >10% p95 latency regression within 60 minutes of apply.
- Maintain full audit trail and traceability for every automated config change.

High-level approach:
1) Continuous profiling: lightweight agents sample request metadata (seq len, model variant, arrival inter-arrival quantiles, prefix hit rate). Profile windows are configurable: default 30-minute rolling windows plus 24-hour aggregate. Profiles stored in telemetry bucket and summarized by workload fingerprint.
2) Heuristic scoring: produce candidate batching/caching configs (microbatch size, batch timeout, enable-prefix-cache, kv-cache-budget) and score using a composite heuristic: cost_delta_estimate, p95_latency_risk, cache-safety (prefix reuse probability), and stability_penalty (recent variance). Heuristics are parameterized and tunable via Confluence doc.
3) Simulation + shadow evaluation: candidates are simulated against collected traces to estimate token-cost and latency distribution. Top candidates are shadow-applied for 1 hour in shadow mode (no live effect) to validate estimates.
4) Guarded apply: staged canary rollout + progressive ramp with circuit-breaker thresholds and automatic rollback. Canary size defaults to 1% of traffic, ramp to 10% after 30m stable, then 50% after 2h. All stages require no safety threshold violations.

Key design choices / trade-offs considered:
- Profiling granularity vs. overhead: chosen 30m windows to balance responsiveness and telemetry cost; per-request capture is sampled at 1/100 for high-throughput workloads.
- Heuristic simplicity vs. ML model: we prefer deterministic heuristics initially to keep behavior transparent to SREs and customers; leave ML-driven scoring for follow-up work.
- Conservative rollout default: prioritizing reliability over aggressive cost wins to reduce risk of customer-visible regressions.

Rollout and safety rules (guarded apply):
- Safety metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, token-per-request, CPU/GPU utilization, cost-per-token estimate.
- Auto-revert triggers: error rate +0.5 percentage-point absolute OR p95 latency +10% absolute OR cost increase of any magnitude with latency regression. Reverts are automatic and produce incident log + Slack alert.
- Manual review gates: applies that target >30% estimated cost reduction or touch >1000 rps workloads require PM+SRE signoff.

Observability and auditability:
- New dashboards: costpilot/workload-scores, costpilot/rollback-audit, op-latency/regressions.
- Each suggested config stored as a versioned artifact with provenance: profiling-window-id, scoring-revision, simulator-run-id, shadow-run-id, and apply-job-id.
- GitHub PR template and Confluence runbook linked below for on-call procedures.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for heuristics and simulator.
- Replay tests using historic traces in staging (replay-runner).
- Canary on dedicated cluster with synthetic traffic + golden traces.
- Chaos exercise: fault-inject increased latency to validate circuit-breaker rollback logic.

Open questions / risks:
- How frequently should candidate scoring hyperparameters be tuned? Initial plan: monthly review.
- Handling multi-tenant workloads where batching config conflicts across customers — recommend per-customer override and conservative defaults.
- Long-tail rare workloads with bursty patterns may produce noisy profiles; we will require a minimum sample size before recommending.

Related artifacts (links):
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COST/CostPilot+Design 
- GitHub draft PR (scoring + simulator): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428
- Shadow-run dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/dashboards/costpilot-shadow

Next milestones:
- 2025-03-07: complete simulator integration and unit test coverage (in progress).
- 2025-03-12: run first full shadow-eval on top 50 workloads.
- 2025-03-15: gated canary rollout to production for low-risk workloads.

Stakeholders: Product (Maya Chen), SRE (Diego Ramos), Security reviewer pending for telemetry retention policy.
